questions.title: Who will lead the 2026 Open Championship after the second round?
questions.background: The Open Championship is one of the four major championships in men's professional golf. The halfway leader is the golfer with the lowest cumulative score over the first two rounds.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The R&A's official second-round leaderboard for the 2026 Open Championship, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the golfer occupying outright first place when the second-round standings are finalized, including any applicable scoring penalties. Accepted Answer Format : The golfer's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-11 Genesis Scottish Open Round 3 (CBS Sports, BBC Sport, Golfmagic; suspended due to thick coastal fog): (1) Co-leader Rory McIlroy stumbled +3 through 8 holes (three-putt bogey on 3, chunked gap wedge on 5, missed <1-foot putt on 7) to drop from T1 to T25 (-6, 5 shots back; Scottish Open odds drifted from +220 to 25-1) and now faces an exhausting 28-hole Sunday marathon right before Open week. Reversing yesterday's overreaction to two Renaissance Club rounds restores World No. 1 and defending Open champion Scottie Scheffler—now getting extra Royal Birkdale practice days after missing the Scottish Open cut—slightly ahead (0.065 -> 0.070 vs McIlroy 0.075 -> 0.068). (2) Major new addition: Englishman Matt Fitzpatrick (World No. 4, 3 PGA Tour wins already in 2026, PGA Tour POY frontrunner, Tour-best 28 straight made cuts) fired -3 through 8 holes in nasty coastal fog to seize T1 (-11, 13/5 Scottish Open favorite), entering #3 at 0.042 ahead of Southport native Tommy Fleetwood (held at 0.038 after finishing R3 solidly at -7, T16) and Jon Rahm (0.032 -> 0.030, finished R3 at -4), replacing Xander Schauffele. Top-5 sum 0.248 preserves 75.2% on the remaining 151-player field ahead of Royal Birkdale's R1/R2 AM-PM Irish Sea weather-wave draw.

local_articles.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang courts Japanese suppliers with pork skewers
local_articles.snippet: TOKYO - On the night of July 15, Jensen Huang was in Tokyo’s central Kanda district courting the little-known Japanese suppliers that underpin the AI supply chain. The Nvidia Corp chief executive officer swept into a cozy izakaya in the area popular for after-work drinks, turning a narrow lane known for grilled pork skewers and beer crates into a theatre for the AI boom. Outside, a crowd pressed in with smartphones raised, hoping for a glimpse of the man they refer to as kawajan-san – Mr Leather Jacket – on social media and whose chips have become central to the global AI race. Inside sat the chiefs of Kioxia Holdings Corp, maker of advanced flash memory chips; Shin-Etsu Chemical Co, the world’s leading provider of advanced silicon wafers; chip gear designer Tokyo Electron Ltd; and Ajinomoto Co, the sole supplier of a film used in leading-edge chip packages. questions.title: Which Gaza locality will be the site of the deadliest Israeli strike reported on July 17, 2026?
questions.background: A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect in October 2025, but Israeli attacks in Gaza have continued.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Al Jazeera's July 17, 2026 reporting on that day's attacks across Gaza. Compare individual strikes rather than cumulative deaths across separate attacks. Resolution Date : 2026-07-17 Accepted Answer Format : Resolve to the city, town, or refugee camp where the individual Israeli strike with the highest reported death toll occurred. Answer with the locality's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Empirical analysis of all 24 unique Al Jazeera Gaza strike articles from June 24 through July 10 shows a clear shift toward southern Gaza tent/residential strikes alongside Gaza City: Gaza City (13 articles; deadliest individual strikes on July 1 killing 3 and July 7 Sabra taxi strike killing 4) and Khan Younis (13 articles; deadliest on June 27, July 9 Batn as-Sameen, and overlapping June 24/July 6/July 8) lead the sample, followed closely by al-Mawasi (8 articles; repeated lethal displacement-tent strikes including July 6 killing 2 and July 8 killing 4 in al-Mawasi/Khan Younis). By contrast, Deir el-Balah (2 articles; deadliest June 29) and Nuseirat (2 articles; 1 killed July 9) appeared much less often, while Beit Lahiya appeared 4 times (June 28 deadliest strike killing 2; July 10 Kamal Adwan Hospital drone attack wounding 6). Updating from the June 24 prior raises Khan Younis (0.22 -> 0.27) and al-Mawasi (0.08 -> 0.13), trims Deir el-Balah (0.12 -> 0.10), Nuseirat (0.10 -> 0.07), and Gaza City (0.28 -> 0.27), and keeps 16% residual for Beit Lahiya, Maghazi, Bureij, Jabalia, and other localities.

local_articles.title: Escalating Israeli strikes kill five people in Gaza, medics say
local_articles.snippet: CAIRO, July 16 - Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on Thursday, Palestinian health officials said, as a U.S.-based research group reported a surge in Israeli attacks to levels not seen since the latest truce took effect in October. Medics said an Israeli airstrike killed two people near the Tuffah neighbourhood in the north of the enclave, while a third person was killed in Israeli tank shelling in the Zeitoun suburb in eastern Gaza City. Another airstrike at a tent encampment for displaced people in western Gaza City killed one person and wounded several, while an attack on a vehicle in Khan Younis, in the south, killed another, medics said. Witnesses also reported that an airstrike hit a residential building in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza. The Israeli military had no immediate comment on any of the incidents.
